{{Short description|Algebraic variety in a Hilbert scheme}}
{{more footnotes|date=June 2019}}

{{About|the moduli space of projective curves|other mathematical objects with the same name|Severi variety (disambiguation){{!}}Severi variety}}
In mathematics, a '''Severi variety''' is an [[algebraic variety]] in a [[Hilbert scheme]] that parametrizes [[projective curve|curves in projective space]] with given degree and [[geometric genus]] and at most [[Singular point of a curve|node singularities]]. Its dimension is 3''d''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''g''&nbsp;−&nbsp;1.

It is a theorem that Severi varieties are [[algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]], i.e. irreducible.{{cn|date=August 2017}}

== References ==
*Maksym Fedorchuk, [https://www2.bc.edu/maksym-fedorchuk/papers/thesis.pdf Severi varieties and the moduli space of curves], Ph.D. thesis, 2008.
*[[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]] and Ian Morrison. ''Moduli of curves,'' volume 187 of Graduate Texts in Mathematics. Springer-Verlag, New York, 1998.
